narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

Mostly clear skies start the day before temperatures rise to a high of 32°C (90°F), dropping to a low of 21°C (70°F) overnight. Early Mostly clear conditions transition to Mostly clear at midday and Mostly cloudy in the evening, with thunder possible, peaking this evening. Winds will be north-northeasterly overnight, turning southwest by midday, with gusts up to 34 km/h (18 kt). The UV index will peak at 8.9. Ground stations report air quality with highest station: Kisumu Airport at AQI 137, 3 of 3 reporting. As of 06:01, reports through 03:00: no rain; no thunder; high so far 23°C (73°F); low so far 22°C (72°F); peak sustained 11 km/h (6 kt); sky partly cloudy.

## Extended Outlook

NEXT THREE DAYS: temperatures and winds much the same through Monday, with thunderstorms likely Saturday and Sunday, and thunderstorms possible Monday. Saturday and Sunday are modelled as partly cloudy, while Monday stays partly cloudy and the rest of the week moves toward mostly cloudy. The models show a slim chance of rain – only one of four models wet each day – with amounts under 1 mm (0.04 in). Highs range from 31°C (88°F) on Saturday to a maximum of 34°C (93°F) on Monday, while lows sit near 19°C (66°F). The record note for Day+3 highlights ECMWF as the best rain record holder.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

Thunderstorms ahead carry the hazard of sudden gusts well above the forecast wind. PEAK CAPE AHEAD values reach 1130 J/kg for GFS, 1420 J/kg for ICON, 2380 J/kg for ECMWF, 2540 J/kg for Best Match, and 5540 J/kg for UKMO, with instability peaking at 18:00. No severe weather warning is active from the local met service.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

On Winam Gulf, winds will be northeasterly overnight at 7 km/h (4 kt) gusting 10 km/h (6 kt), then southwesterly by midday at 4 km/h (2 kt) gusting 14 km/h (7 kt), then west-southwesterly into the evening at 12 km/h (6 kt) gusting 21 km/h (11 kt); peak gust 25 km/h (14 kt). Sudden gusts well above the forecast wind are a hazard with any thunderstorm.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the north (1009 hPa) and highest toward the northeast (1016 hPa) — a 6 hPa spread, a moderate large-scale gradient. Pressure is also falling toward the south, southeast — a large-scale feature building in that direction, though this sampling cannot say how fast or whether it will reach here. Pressure overhead is near-steady. Sampling is a nine-point ring at 12-degree spacing, so this locates a direction, not a centre or a front. Across 5 points, today's mean sea-level pressure sits between 1012.1 and 1014.5 hPa; near-steady over three days (-0.3 hPa). The pressure trend shows -0.7 hPa.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

At Day+0, no model is meaningfully better than the others here yet, while ECMWF holds the best rain record at 87% right over the last 30 checks. Best Match slightly under-forecasts daytime highs here, yet projects 32.4°C (90.3°F) today against the call's 32°C (90°F), standing higher than GFS at 31°C (88°F), ECMWF at 31.1°C (88.0°F), UKMO at 31.3°C (88.3°F), and ICON at 30.8°C (87.4°F). ECMWF systematically under-forecasts peak wind, calling 22.3 km/h (12 kt) against Best Match at 43.2 km/h (23 kt) and the call at 34 km/h (18 kt). Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) forecasts a high of 31°C (88°F) and low of 22°C (72°F) with sunny intervals and partly cloudy skies, agreeing with the dry call but sitting slightly cooler on daytime high. DATA SUFFICIENCY shows 103 reviewed days with 74 checks for the least-covered model at Day+0, giving a settled picture, though KMD has fewer checks than the other models.

extended_outlook:
Temperatures and winds much the same through Monday, with thunderstorms likely Saturday and Sunday, and thunderstorms possible Monday. Skies partly cloudy throughout. Monday's call: dry, 32%, with one of four models wet; highs around 32°C (90°F). Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) calls it dry. At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 93% of the time over 100 checks.

Further out, cooling through Friday, with thunderstorms likely Tuesday and Wednesday, showers and thunderstorms possible Thursday, and dry Friday with thunderstorms possible. Tuesday: one of four models wet, highs 32 to 34°C (89 to 94°F), thunder likely rather than possible. Wednesday: one of four models wet, highs 31 to 33°C (88 to 92°F). Thursday: all three models that reach it wet, the week's wettest day at 4 mm (0.16 in) on average, highs 29 to 32°C (85 to 89°F), thunder possible rather than likely.

Only GFS, ECMWF and ICON reach past Wednesday. Friday's call: dry, 0%, with no model wet; highs around 30°C (86°F). At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 93% of the time over 96 checks.
